summary: Dipak Ranjan Das worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Dineschandra Sircar and held a post in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

Dipesh Chakrabarty works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at Presidency College, Kolkata, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University under Donald Anthony Low. He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1984–1995) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago (1995).

Dirk H. A. Kolff is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his MA and doctorate at Leiden University, where he taught at the Kern Institute (1967–1991) and held the Chair of Indian History (1991–2003).

Divyaraj Amiya is an Indology and linguistics scholar. His career includes posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich (both attested 2026).

Diwakar Acharya is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Ramananda Giri and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg. He taught at Nepal Sanskrit University, Hamburg, and Kyoto University before becoming a professor at Oxford in 2016.
Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu. He served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dmitry Kudryavsky was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at St. Petersburg University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev between ~1885 and 1890, and held a post at the Imperial University of Dorpat from ~1898 to 1918.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under numerous teachers, including Menpa Bum Rampa Tendzin Döndrub, Kunzang Pelden, and Dzongsar Khyentse 02, and taught scholars and figures such as Ronald M. Davidson and Tulku Thondup.

Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and studied with S. A. Srinivasan. He has held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient since 2000 and lectured at EPHE in 2005.

Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen Christina Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chonam, and held a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist who studied at the University of London and University of Oxford. His career includes positions at the Wellcome Institute (~1985–2002), University College London (2002–2009), the University of Vienna (2009–2015), and the University of Alberta (2015).

Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who completed his studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1978–1984). He has held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles since around 1987.

Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and held a post as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don Alvin Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who was a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago. He served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, he served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from ~1972 to 2006.

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indologist, linguist, and historian. Educated at Richmond College and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, he worked as an epigraphist for the Government of Sri Lanka (~1899–1929) and at the University of London (~1918–1930).

Donald A. Ringe is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Kentucky, Oxford, and Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill. After teaching Classics at Bard College (1983–1985), he joined the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

Donald Anthony Low was a historian and Indologist who studied at Exeter College and Clare Hall, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the Australian National University (~1959–1982), the University of Sussex (~1964–1972), and the University of Cambridge (~1983–1994).

Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John C. Y. Wang and Akira Takeda, and held a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (attested 1989).

Donald Eric Capps was a religious studies scholar educated at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago, North Carolina at Charlotte, and Phillips University before serving at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).
